subject: general
question: How much clearance is to be provided for compression ring fitted into the piston of an IC engine?

options.text: 0.002 D to 0.004 D where D is the cylinder bore

solution:
The correct answer is __0.002 D to 0.004 D where D is the cylinder bore**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Compression ring clearance__ is a critical aspect of IC engine design.
 
• It is typically specified as a fraction of the cylinder bore diameter (D).
 
• The recommended clearance range is 0.002 D to 0.004 D.
 
• This precise clearance ensures optimal sealing and reduces the risk of engine damage.
 
• Excessive clearance may result in leakage or reduced efficiency, while insufficient clearance could lead to ring seizure.
 
• Proper clearance contributes to the engine's performance and longevity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Piston Rings:**

 
 
• Piston rings are crucial components of an IC engine, serving to seal the combustion chamber.
 
• They prevent the leakage of combustion gases and regulate oil consumption.
 
 
 
• **Compression Rings:**
 
 
• Compression rings are located at the top of the piston and are primarily responsible for sealing the combustion chamber.
 
• They are designed to withstand high temperatures and pressures.
 
 
 
• **Oil Control Rings:**
 
 
• These rings regulate the amount of oil that passes between the piston and cylinder walls.
 
• They help maintain proper lubrication while preventing excessive oil consumption.
